We are a curious and motivated team with a shared interest in science, technology, mathematics and space exploration. Our strengths include logical thinking, creativity and problem-solving. We enjoy learning new things, exchanging ideas and approaching challenges from different perspectives.

Through the NASA Space Apps Challenge, we want to gain practical experience, develop innovative ideas and turn our curiosity into meaningful solutions.
summary:
LUNASITE is an interactive 3D platform that helps users evaluate and compare potential landing sites at the Moon’s South Pole. Designed to support future Artemis and Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) missions, it combines lunar topography, astronomical calculations and mission simulations to assess the safety and practicality of different landing locations.

Users can explore the lunar surface, select candidate landing sites, simulate different dates and launch delays, and examine important mission conditions such as solar illumination, communication visibility, terrain slope and proximity to potential water-ice deposits.

The platform also includes an automated site recommendation system that ranks locations according to mission requirements. By making complex lunar data easier to explore and understand, LUNASITE supports more informed decisions about future lunar exploration.

Github link: https://github.com/dzxtckfdd/lunar_landing_space_navigator
details:
The problem

The lunar South Pole is an important destination for future exploration because permanently shadowed regions may contain water ice and other valuable resources. However, landing in this region presents significant challenges. Extreme lighting conditions, long periods of darkness, difficult terrain and limited communication visibility can put missions at risk.

Our solution

LUNASITE provides an interactive environment for analysing potential landing locations. Its main features include:

  • 3D lunar exploration: Explore the Moon and inspect potential landing regions.
  • Date and time simulation: Investigate how lighting and celestial positions change over time.
  • Terrain and horizon analysis: Examine surrounding terrain and potential obstructions.
  • Mission condition monitoring: Evaluate sunlight availability, communication windows and periods of darkness.
  • Launch-delay simulation: Test how changes to a planned launch date affect mission conditions.
  • Automated site recommendations: Compare candidate locations using mission-specific constraints and ranking criteria.

How it works

Users select a lunar region or place a custom location on the 3D Moon. They can then choose a date and time to evaluate the site's conditions. The platform combines astronomical calculations with terrain information to estimate illumination and Earth visibility. Its recommendation engine compares candidate locations according to selected mission requirements.

Expected impact

LUNASITE aims to make lunar landing-site analysis more accessible and understandable. It can serve as an educational and exploratory decision-support tool for students, researchers and people interested in space exploration. It also demonstrates how open planetary data can be transformed into practical tools for future missions.
